newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei shed gains, end flat ahead Fed meet.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei shed gains, end flat ahead Fed meet.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures gave up most of their early gains on Tuesday and ended steady in a thin market as players awaited the rates decision by U.S. Federal Reserve policymakers due later in the day.
Dealers said the market had priced in a 25-basis-point hike in the Fed funds rate, but anything above that could give a boost to the dollar, and consequently the Nikkei.
Worries about the Bank of Japan following suit if the Fed raised rates have faded, as players do not expect the Japanese central bank to tighten credit before the end of the year.
After hitting a high of 21,280, the benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract came off to close at 21,155 against a previous settlement at 21,150. Volume remained low at 10,300 lots.
"There was a little early selling but it was very well absorbed. Sentiment's still bullish," said one trader.
He said the market was likely to trade sideways in a range of 21,050 to 21,480-21,500 in the near term.
"It's not a market to look to sell. It's more a market to wait to buy," he said, adding that bargain hunters were likely to buoy the index on any moves down towards 21,000.
